plain: Running slower can actually help you run faster over time through a training method built around building aerobic capacity without overtaxing your body. When you run at an easy, conversational pace, often called "zone 2" training, your body becomes more efficient at using oxygen and burning fat for fuel, strengthening your heart, capillaries, and mitochondria at the cellular level. This creates a stronger aerobic base that supports faster running later, since a bigger aerobic engine means you can sustain higher speeds before your body switches to less efficient anaerobic energy systems. Slower running also reduces injury risk and recovery time compared to constant high-intensity training, letting you train more consistently and accumulate more total mileage over weeks and months. Elite runners spend most of their training at easy paces, saving hard efforts for specific workouts.
